section: 13.5 Every handler is an idempotent receiver
text: Helland's "Life beyond Distributed Transactions" makes it a rule: between entities that share no transaction, messages may arrive more than once, so every recipient must be idempotent. In his words, "any message ever sent may be delivered multiple times" (section 5, "Activities: Coping with Messy Messages", under "Retries and Idempotence").
author: Pat Helland
title: Life beyond Distributed Transactions: an Apostate's Opinion
locator: section 1 "Most Applications Use 'At-Least-Once' Messaging" / "Entities Manage Per-Partner State"; section 5 "Activities: Coping with Messy Messages", "Retries and Idempotence"
verification: Re-verified 2026-11-06 against the live source (curl + pdftotext/grep, or browser). cidr07p15.pdf section 5 "Retries and Idempotence".
evidence: "Retries and Idempotence. Since any message ever sent may be delivered multiple times, we need a discipline in the application to cope with repeated messages." ... "Recall the assumption that messages are delivered 'at-least-once'. This means that the recipient entity must be prepared in its durable state to be assailed with redundant messages that must be ignored."
